cards.explanation: The answer is quarreling over words. Paul says to charge the believers before God to avoid quarreling over words (2 Timothy 2:14). You know the kind, friends. It starts over one little word and ends with somebody muting the group chat. Paul says to steer clear of it.

The answer is ruin. Paul says quarreling over words succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin (2 Timothy 2:14). Notice it's the listeners, friends. They're the ones who end up hurt by all that arguing. That's why Paul charges the believers before God to avoid it.

The answer is the word of truth. Paul wants Timothy to be an unashamed workman who accurately handles it. I handle my dough with care, friends, and this is way more important than dough. A good workman respects what's in his hands.

The answer is spread. Paul says the talk of such men will spread like gangrene (2 Timothy 2:17). He's talking about the men he's just described, who speak irreverent, empty chatter. Their talk doesn't stay in one spot, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says Hymenaeus and Philetus claim the resurrection has already occurred (2 Timothy 2:18). He names them and he names what they say, friends. That's the teaching he says has deviated from the truth.

The answer is undermining their faith. Paul says Hymenaeus and Philetus undermine the faith of some (2 Timothy 2:18). Think of pulling out the bottom cookie from a tall stack, friends. Everything above it starts to wobble.

The answer is, The Lord knows those who are His. That's the first saying on the seal of God's firm foundation (2 Timothy 2:19). Some people's faith may be shaking, friends, but the foundation stands. He knows His own.

The answer is iniquity. The seal says, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.” (2 Timothy 2:19) Calling on the Lord comes with turning away, friends. Both halves of that seal belong together.

The answer is True. Paul says some vessels are for honorable use, but others are for common use (2 Timothy 2:20). Every house needs both kinds, friends. Even a kitchen has the nice platter and the everyday mixing bowl.

The answer is cleansing himself of what is unfit. Paul says if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor (2 Timothy 2:21). It's about being cleansed, friends, not about being fancy. Anybody can be that kind of vessel.

The answer is prepared for every good work. Paul says the vessel for honor is sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work (2 Timothy 2:21). That's an apron-on, oven-hot kind of readiness, friends. Ready for whatever good work comes in.

The answer is others who call on the Lord from a pure heart. Paul says to pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart (2 Timothy 2:22). Timothy isn't pictured chasing them alone, friends. He's pictured alongside others who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

The answer is False. Paul says a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing (2 Timothy 2:24). Quarrelsome is the one thing he rules out, friends. I'd put that line up on my own bakery wall.

The answers are kind and teach. Paul says a servant of the Lord must be kind to everyone, friends, not just the people who agree with him. That's a wide circle. Paul also says the servant must be able to teach. That's a skill that goes right alongside the kindness, showing somebody how without making them feel small.

The answer is gently. Paul says the servant must gently reprove those who oppose him (2 Timothy 2:25). He says it's in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth. Think of pressing a cookie stamp, friends. Gentle is the word Paul picks.
The answer is repentance. Paul says to reprove in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth. Notice who grants it, friends. The hope is that God may grant it.

The answer is the snare of the devil. Paul says they will come to their senses and escape it, since the devil has taken them captive to his will (2 Timothy 2:26). A snare is a trap, friends, and they get out of it. That's good news, and it starts with God granting repentance.
